library(ggplot2)

snapshot_date <- "2026-11-18"

read_snapshot <- function(file, ...) {

  if (file.exists(local_file)) read.csv(local_file, ...) else read.csv(paste0(snapshot_site, file), ...)
}
data_date <- snapshot_date

## 1. The genes in human mtDNA (given)

This chunk downloads the feature table of the human mitochondrial genome,
[NC_012920.1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/NC_012920.1), and turns it into
one row per gene. You do not need to change it.

```{r genes}
# Turn an NCBI feature table into one row per CDS, tRNA or rRNA gene
parse_feature_table <- function(text) {
  lines <- strsplit(text, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  features <- list()
  for (line in lines[-1]) {
    cells <- strsplit(line, "\t", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    if (length(cells) >= 3 && nzchar(cells[1]) && nzchar(cells[3])) {
      features[[length(features) + 1]] <- list(start = as.integer(cells[1]),
        end = as.integer(cells[2]), type = cells[3], gene = "", product = "")
    } else if (length(cells) >= 5 && cells[4] %in% c("gene", "product")) {
      features[[length(features)]][[cells[4]]] <- cells[5]
    }
  }
  tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(features, as.data.frame))
  gene_rows <- tab[tab$type == "gene", ]
  out <- tab[tab$type %in% c("CDS", "tRNA", "rRNA"), ]
  key <- function(x) paste(x$start, x$end)
  out$gene <- gene_rows$gene[match(key(out), key(gene_rows))]
  out$strand <- ifelse(out$start < out$end, "+", "-")
  lo <- pmin(out$start, out$end); hi <- pmax(out$start, out$end)
  out$start <- lo; out$end <- hi
  # Which respiratory complex does each protein-coding gene belong to?
  out$complex <- "RNA"
  out$complex[grepl("^ND", out$gene)] <- "I"
  out$complex[out$gene == "CYTB"] <- "III"
  out$complex[grepl("^COX", out$gene)] <- "IV"
  out$complex[grepl("^ATP", out$gene)] <- "V"
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out[, c("gene", "start", "end", "strand", "type", "complex", "product")]
}

if (use_snapshot) {
  genes <- read_snapshot("mtdna-features-2026-11-18.csv")
} else {
  genes <- tryCatch({
    ncbi_url <- paste0("https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi",
                       "?db=nuccore&id=NC_012920.1&rettype=ft&retmode=text")
    raw <- paste(readLines(ncbi_url, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
    data_date <- as.character(Sys.Date())
    parse_feature_table(raw)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("NCBI did not answer; using the course snapshot.")
    read_snapshot("mtdna-features-2026-11-18.csv")
  })
}
head(genes)
```

## 2. Mitochondrial proteins in UniProt (given)

All reviewed human proteins that UniProt places in the mitochondrion.

```{r proteins}
uniprot_url <- paste0("https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/stream?format=tsv",
  "&fields=accession,gene_primary",
  "&query=organism_id%3A9606%20AND%20reviewed%3Atrue%20AND%20cc_scl_term%3ASL-0173")

if (use_snapshot) {
  mito_proteins <- read_snapshot("uniprot-mitochondria-2026-11-18.csv", check.names = FALSE)
} else {
  mito_proteins <- tryCatch(read.delim(uniprot_url, check.names = FALSE),
    error = function(e) {
      message("UniProt did not answer; using the course snapshot.")
      read_snapshot("uniprot-mitochondria-2026-11-18.csv", check.names = FALSE)
    })
}
n_mito <- nrow(mito_proteins)
n_mito
percent_mtdna <- round(100 * 13 / n_mito, 1)
percent_mtdna
```

UniProt lists `r n_mito` mitochondrial proteins. Only 13 are encoded in mtDNA,
that is `r percent_mtdna` %.

## 3. Example plot: genes by type (given)

```{r example-plot, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot(genes, aes(x = type)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Gene type", y = "Number of genes", title = "Genes in human mtDNA")
```

## 4. Your plot: protein genes by respiratory complex

Solution: the three blanks are filled.

```{r your-plot, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.5}
# Blank 1: keep only the protein-coding genes (the gene type that makes proteins)
protein_genes <- genes[genes$type == "CDS", ]

# Blank 2: the column to count on the x axis
# Blank 3: a label for the x axis (text in quotes)
ggplot(protein_genes, aes(x = complex)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Respiratory complex", y = "Number of mtDNA-encoded subunits",
       title = "mtDNA-encoded subunits per complex")
```

Data: NCBI NC_012920.1 and UniProtKB, retrieved `r data_date`.
